Midterm elections usually go against sitting presidents. Only four times since 1902 has the president’s party gained congressional seats in the midterms, with Bush the last to do so in 2002 after the 9/11 terrorist attacks.

Trump’s polling shows an approval rating of -23 per cent, with 60 per cent of Americans disapproving of his performance in office. This is fairly typical for recent presidents, with support declining throughout their term in office.
